beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact recurrent thought process updates windowed tokens before decoding.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The method keeps spatial detail in a carrier while the thought process stays compact. The encoder first maps the low-resolution image into dense features. The features are partitioned into windows without dropping tokens. DQ-CTM reads and updates the window tokens over repeated ticks. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into the high-resolution image. The thought stage recurs on itself, and its parameters are shared across ticks.

params.headline: ThinkSR updates dense windows with a shared recurrent thought stage
params.note: The loop belongs to the thought stage, not the whole flow.

beats.intent: The carrier equation says dense features come from the encoder, then window partitioning preserves every token for thought updates.
beats.narration: The carrier starts as a dense feature field, not as a compact state. The encoder transforms the low-resolution image into that field. The window operator partitions the field while keeping every token available to the recurrent process.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded first, then partitioned into windows

terms.label: encoder from low-resolution image to dense feature field
window partition that keeps every token

beats.intent: Among the five benchmarked methods, DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model; its 1.129 million parameters are second largest.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison should be read as a cost, not as a win for compactness. CATANet is the smallest reported model at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN is close behind at 0.550 million. IMDN reports 0.715 million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR reports 1.129 million, making it the second largest of these five. CARN is the largest at 1.592 million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is the second largest model in the benchmark table
params.note: Sorted by parameter count, smallest first.
